draft.title: Scams and identity theft
card: a trick to get money or personal details from a person. Common types include fake online shops, phishing messages and fake prizes.
when someone uses another person's stolen details, such as a name, birth date or bank details, to pretend to be them. They may open accounts or buy things in that person's name.
Scams often add pressure, such as "act now" or "you have won". A message that asks for details you did not expect to be asked for is a warning sign.
Consumers can guard against both by checking a seller is real before paying. They should also never share passwords or codes, even with someone who says they are from a bank.
draft.remember: A scam tricks you into giving up money or details. Identity theft misuses those details. Check sellers and keep passwords private.

a.q: Jai gets a text saying a parcel is held and he must click a link and enter his bank details. The text is from an unknown sender. What is the best description of it?
opts: A scam that tries to trick him into giving details
A refund offered by a real delivery company
Identity theft that has already been carried out
A fair deal that he can trust if he acts quickly
a.why: The text tries to trick Jai into handing over his bank details, so it is a scam. It is not yet identity theft, because nothing has been used. That would only start if the criminals used his details to pretend to be him.
a.clue: Has anyone used Jai's details yet, or are they trying to get them?

b.q: Priya finds a bank loan in her name that she never applied for. The lender used her name, birth date and address. What has most likely happened?
opts: Identity theft, as someone used her stolen details
A scam, as she was tricked into buying a product
A consumer guarantee, as the loan was unfit for purpose
A refund, as the lender chose to repair the loan
b.why: Someone used Priya's personal details to pretend to be her and take out a loan, which is identity theft. A scam would involve her being tricked into handing over money or details herself, and she was not told of this at all.
b.clue: Did someone trick Priya, or did someone act in her name?

a.best: A scam that tries to trick him into giving details

b.best: Identity theft, as someone used her stolen details

problems.detail: The why's last clause, 'she was not told of this at all', is confusing. The stem gives no sign she was tricked, so it should say something like 'nothing suggests she was tricked into handing anything over'.

The stem says 'The lender used her name, birth date and address', which could suggest the lender itself misused her details. Wording such as 'The loan was taken out using her name...' would be clearer.
